record.paper_title: Unfolding the Labyrinth: Open Problems in Physics, Mathematics, Astrophysics and Other Areas of Science
record.original_question: How many nontrivial integer solutions does x^3 + y^3 + z^3 = 1 have beyond the explicit examples listed in the source, and more generally how many solutions are there to A x^3 + B y^3 + C z^3 = D, or even to A1 x1^3 + A2 x2^3 + ... + An xn^3 = B, under the coprimality assumptions stated there?

evidence.quote: How many other nontrivial integer solutions are there?
As a generalization, how many solutions has the equation: Ax + By + Cz = D 3 3 3

artifact.self_contained_problem:
(a) Determine all nontrivial integer solutions (x, y, z) ∈ ℤ³ to the Diophantine equation
    x³ + y³ + z³ = 1.
In particular, classify the parametric families of solutions and decide whether all integer solutions are accounted for by a finite list of polynomial parametrizations.

(b) More generally, for fixed nonzero integers A, B, C, D with gcd(A, B, C, D) = 1 (and gcd(A, B, C) coprime to D in the natural sense so that local obstructions are excluded), describe and count the integer solutions (x, y, z) ∈ ℤ³ of
    A x³ + B y³ + C z³ = D.

(c) For each integer n ≥ 3, fixed nonzero integers A₁, …, Aₙ, B with gcd(A₁, …, Aₙ, B) = 1, study the integer solutions (x₁, …, xₙ) ∈ ℤⁿ of
    A₁ x₁³ + A₂ x₂³ + ⋯ + Aₙ xₙ³ = B,
and provide either an asymptotic count of solutions of bounded height or a description of all solutions via parametric families.
artifact.status_search_result: The classification of all integer solutions to x³ + y³ + z³ = 1 (and more generally A x³ + B y³ + C z³ = D and its n-variable analogues) is widely regarded as open. While infinitely many solutions to x³ + y³ + z³ = 1 are known via several polynomial parametric families (e.g., Mahler's family (9t⁴)³ + (1 − 9t³)³ + (3t − 9t⁴)³ = 1 and others catalogued by Rowland), it is not known whether every integer solution lies in finitely many such families. The general question of describing or counting integer solutions to ternary cubic forms A x³ + B y³ + C z³ = D, and the higher-variable generalizations, remains an active and largely unresolved problem in Diophantine number theory.

status_evidence.title: Known families of integer solutions of x^3+y^3+z^3=n
status_evidence.snippet: Catalogue of known polynomial parametric families for x^3+y^3+z^3=n; completeness is not established.
status_evidence.claim: Several parametric families for x^3+y^3+z^3=1 are known but it is unknown whether they cover all solutions.

status_evidence.title: Sums of three cubes (Sutherland)
status_evidence.snippet: For k not of the form m^3 or 2m^3 and k not ≡ ±4 (mod 9), the existence and distribution of solutions to x^3+y^3+z^3=k is largely open.
status_evidence.claim: Counting and classifying integer solutions of x^3+y^3+z^3=k remains open for most k.

status_evidence.title: On the smallest open Diophantine equations
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses status of small cubic Diophantine equations, many of which remain open.
status_evidence.claim: Many ternary cubic Diophantine equations are open problems.
